title: The early-childhood grant system: $340,000 approved in 2021, $3.3 million in 2023
question: What did the commission approve for its sole-source grant-management system, and what does the same agreement carry now?
finding: In May 2021 the commission approved a contract with Cityspan Technologies for up to $340,000 from July 2021 through June 2026 (a base of $60,000 a year plus a one-time migration), described in the minutes as a sole source. The same agreement number (1000022730) now carries an agreed amount of $2.2 million in the City's supplier-contracts table; $1.1 million has been paid on it, $830,000 of that in fiscal 2026 and 2027 under the title 'DEC FY26 Contract Mgt System'. That is inside a later approval: on June 7, 2023 the commission approved an amendment for a total not to exceed $3.3 million from July 2021 through June 2028, for a new contract-management system for the Department of Early Childhood; the motion carried unanimously. Nothing unusual remains in the amounts; the contract is still a sole source.
how: The first approval and its terms are read from the May 2021 minutes; the later approval from the draft minutes of 7 June 2023, printed in the packet for the meeting of 4 October 2023 (whether that meeting adopted them as drafted was not checked). Payments are every voucher line to the payee on each of its agreements, by year label; the agreed amount is the sum of the supplier-contracts rows for the agreement number.
limits: The Department of Early Childhood took over First 5's work in 2022 and widened the system to its whole grant portfolio under the 2023 approval. Software licences are exempt from bidding under the City's purchasing rules (the payment lines cite the Administrative Code). The youth and human-services departments buy from the same company on their own agreements, shown for comparison.
